title: First words
story: Bilal meets you at the airport. Your very first Urdu words — just four at a time.
description: Hello, thank you, yes, no — and the words for "I", "you", "this" and "that".

lessons.title: Hello & thank you
lessons.objective: Learn 4 words you will use every single day.

phrases.note: A traditional, respectful Urdu greeting you can say to anyone, often with a small raise of the hand. Say it: aa-DAAB.
Long "aa", and the n is soft — air through your nose.
The n at the end is soft, through the nose: na-hee(n).
Ji is a polite "yes" — like "yes, sir / yes, ma'am". Pakistanis use it all the time.
The "th" is t + a puff of air. It is NOT the "th" in "think".
Also means "oh, I see!" when you say it like a question.
The "kh" is a soft scrape in the throat, like Scottish "loch".
Sounds close to "meh(n)" — the n is just air through the nose.
The polite "you". Use it with everyone you don't know well.

guide.title: Roman Urdu
guide.body: In this app Urdu is first written with English letters ("Roman Urdu") so you can start right away. The real Urdu script is shown underneath — you can look at it, but you don't need to read it yet.

guide.title: Ji makes it polite
guide.body: Haan means yes, but ji (or ji haan) is the polite yes. Use ji with anyone older than you or anyone you don't know.

guide.title: "Aap" is "you"
guide.body: Aap is the respectful word for "you". There are less polite ones, but aap is always safe.
